content:
Table staging.property_rent — Record-grain NSW rental bond lodgements. Physical table: staging.property_rent, matching raw.property_rent and marts.property_rent for easy lineage. One row per bond, cleaned and typed from raw.property_rent (all 5 raw columns are used; nothing was left out). Same role as staging.property_sales — the clean mirror of raw.property_rent. Most questions are better answered by marts.property_rent; use this table for record-level questions raw.property_rent's own columns can answer, e.g. "2-bedroom vs 3-bedroom rent in a suburb". Always filter by postcode and/or rent_month first — this table is ~3M rows. Belongs to the `nsw_rent` dataset (RLS-scoped).
Columns:
  rent_id — Surrogate key, unique per row (raw.property_rent has no natural id column, and two distinct bonds can legitimately share every other value).
  rent_date — Full lodgement date.
  rent_year — Calendar year of rent_date.
  rent_month — First-of-month date, rent_date truncated to month. Join key across sales/rent (with postcode and property_type).
  postcode — Postcode. Join key across sales/rent (with property_type and rent_month).
  property_type_code — Raw source code (H/T/F/U/O) before standardisation — see property_type for the standardised value.
  property_type — 'house' (House/Townhouse) or 'unit' (Flat/Unit/Other). Standardised identically to staging.property_sales.property_type so the two can be joined.
  bedrooms — Bedroom count, where the source value was numeric.
  bedroom_band — Bedroom band: '0','1','2','3','4','5+', or 'unknown' (null bedrooms). Use this for consistent bedroom breakdowns; marts.property_rent is grouped on it.
  weekly_rent — Weekly rent (AUD). Filtered to positive values only.
